The law provides: "That no part of this appropriation, or any other appropriation provided for herein except appropriations made pursuant to treaties, shall be used to educate children of less than one-fourth Indian blood whose parents are citizens of the United States and of the State wherein they live and where there are adequate free-school facilities provided and the facilities of the Indian schools are needed for pupils of more than one-fourth Indian blood." EXTRACTS FROM SCHOOL RULES. If the facilities of a school are not needed as provided in the above paragraph, children showing any Indian blood, whose parents live on an Indian reservation, and who if debarred from Government schools could not obtain an education, may be enrolled in the day and boarding schools of their reservation; children, however, may not be transferred to nonreservation schools without special permission of the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. Before enrolling a pupil superintendents must satisfy themselves whether he has left any other school without permission and whether he has been expelled for cause from any other school. A pupil who has been expelled for cause from any Indian school may be reenrolled in any Indian school only with permission of the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. Attention is invited to Circulars Nos. 1039 and 1044, which must be observed. "The Secretary of the Interior may in his discretion withhold rations, clothing, and other annuities from Indian parents or guardians who refuse or neglect to send or keep their children of proper school age in some school during a reasonable portion of each year." (27 Stat. L., 635. See 2 Dec. Comp., 308.) Gusman Trade School Tacoma Wash. Oct. 6, 1919 Dear Mr. Hammond, Just like to say few words in regard of money I have made so much money this summer and I have old grandfather and mother to look after so its only why I can't very well pay my schooling at Gusman Trade School. I would glad to do that, if I had the money but you know how it is. Mr. Hammond you have showed me your kindness of taken me in school. I am thanking you for it. From Wells Jones. DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR UNITED STATES INDIAN SERVICE SALEM INDIAN TRAINING SCHOOL CHEMAWA, OREGON 9/23/1918 Dear Friend, Just a word to say in regard to my schooling. I came down here to C.L.S. and find things out about the school very good. I think I can getting along better here than up there, because I know I would like it. I know you wish to have me back but in my part I like to stay in Chemawa. I wish you let me stay here. From Wells Jones. Ans. To Wells Jones At C. Oregon Kasaan Alaska Sept. 6, 1914 Dear Friend, Just a word in regard of the letter you wrote me, I am glad that you have interest in me yet. I have served my term at Gusikman, so I think I am not going there. I am thinking about going to C.I. & I think I like it better. I will be down there some time and talk it over. From Della Jones Kassan Alaska Aug. 17 1919 Dear Sir, Your letter was at hand, I was more than glad to hear from you, because I was just wondering what you think of me, after leaving school like that. This letter shows me that you have still interest in me, I wish you would forgive me for all what I have done. I thought I would have better time if I'm out of school but I didn't. I see that now I have no time to write a letter, even work in Sunday. I might go down there, if nothing wrong with me this fall. I keep myself busy every day to make enough to go down and some for the winter spending. I have not much to say. Tell all the teacher I say hello and good luck. From Wells Jones. Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., Aug. 27, 1919 Mr. Wells Jones Kasaan, Alaska My dear Wells: I received your letter of August 17th and am glad that you realize that you made a mistake in leaving school as you did. I sent you a catalog for the 1920 school year and invite your attention to the regulations governing the admission of new pupils. Your application for enrollment was not properly signed by you. I am returning you the old form and a new form to be properly filled out and signed by you with full information concerning the public school facilities available. Very truly yours, Superintendent. EHH:MC Enc. 2 S.S. Alaska Dec. 22, 1918 Dear Friend, I am just about home. The trip was very good, and also the weather, but I never forget the old school yet. I wish you had held your big heart and sent me my mail if I got any at the school. I wish you all have a good luck and a happy New Year. God bless you all. From Wells Jones Address Kascan Alaska Seattle Wash. Butlera Hotel. Dec. 27/918 My Dear Friend, Just a word or so to let you know my troubles, as I tell you that I have a brother here, he is going home so I am gone with him, I am sorry to do all that but I have to. I didn't even ask or let anybody know that I was going home. I did that because I don't like the school this year. I am going on the boat Alaska at 9 A.M. 27 of this month. If you write to Kasaan Alaska, I'll be home day before New Year. From. Wells Jones If you write to Joe, have her tell her all about me. I thought I was going to see her but she didn't, so I have nothing. I wish you have a happy time and happy New Year. Seattle Wash. Butlar Hotel. Dec. 27, 1918 Mr. Thompson, Just a word or so, to let you know my troubles, you know I come over to Seattle to visit my brother. I get into an awful thing he wants me to go home with him so I am going to, I am very sorry that I didn't let you know that or my brother didn't let me know a thing about it. I wish you don't trouble yourself about me, I guess you know that I didn't like school this year. I think you know where I'm going to home. Forgive me for doing that. I wasn't intending to do that but my brother got hold of me. I guess the Supt. will feel sorry about it, I wish you tell him all about it and tell him not to feel trouble about it. He know that I didn't like the school. I ask him two time but he didn't let me go. I have some clothing in my room. I wish you let Willie Hoyle have it. From Wells Jones Don't write till I write again. Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. Oct. 24, 1918. Secretary, Local Board No. 4, Ketchikan, Alaska, Dear Sir: Replying to your letter of October 18, 1918 relative to the correct age of Wells Matthew Jones, you are advised that our records of September, 1915, shows that he was born August 28, 1897. This was the date given on his enrollment blank at that time. Wells says that the only information he has that he is only 21 years of age, is that which he has obtained from his mother. He says that if there is any proof that he is 23 years of age, he has no objection to being classed as of that age. His registration card is returned herewith with no correction in his age being made upon it. Very respectfully, Superintendent K-S Ketchikan, Alaska, October 18, 1918. Mr. Ernest H. Hammond, Superintendent, Cushman Indian Training School, Tacoma, Washington. Sir: We are returning herewith registration card of WELLS MATTHEW JONES. We are informed by his brother that he is about 23 years old. We would thank you to find out his correct age and make correction on card, as this is essential in determining his proper class. Respectfully, LOCAL BOARD No. 4 Ketchikan, Alaska By [signature] Secretary Information regarding pupils to test eligibility and whether in need of Federal aid. Kasaan Alaska Aug. 39, 1918 My Dear Friend, I received your letter which you have wrote me. I was very glad to know that the school is going next term again. I will try to go back there if I don't get called to the service. Wells Jones told me he receive a letter to, and I ask him if he is going down and he told me he didn't make enough money to go down to Cushman. From Wells Jones. I'll be there some day. Kasaan Alaska 5/19/1918 Dear Friend, Just a word, I am home now, and everything is good and also myself. Say my father told me he sent me $30.00, and I left there before I got it so if it there I wish you sent it back to Kasaan clock. I am work now, I think I am going to get along fine.
